newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria pumps 369 mln barrels crude in 1st half 96.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria pumps 369 mln barrels crude in 1st half 96.

text.p: Nigeria produced 369.46 million barrels of crude oil and condensates (2.03 million barrels per day) in the first six months of this year, the national news agency reported on Wednesday.

Production was 8.2 percent higher than that in the corresponding period of last year and two percent higher than in the second half of 1995, the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) said, quoting the Central Bank's half-year economic report.
Total export of crude and condensates during the period under review was 324.23 million barrels, an increase of 12.15 percent over the first half of 1995.
The report said crude deliveries to domestic and offshore refineries declined to 45.5 million barrels, an 11.2 percent fall compared with the corresponding period in 1995, NAN said.
Of the total deliveries, 32.76 million barrels or 72 percent went to domestic refineries.

NAN said during the period, the average price of Nigeria's reference crude, Bonny Light, was $19.07, an increase of $1.87 and $3.17 per barrel over the respective levels in the first and second halves of 1995.
Gas output rose to 17,655.6 million cubic metres in the period under review, a 7.9 and 6.3 percent increase over the respective levels in the first and second halves of 1995.
Most of Nigeria's natural gas, produced during the pumping of crude, is flared.
Nigeria is Africa's leading producer of oil and derives more than 90 percent of its foreign earnings from crude exports.
